originality.rationale: The paper model, qualitative degree dilution, clustering/rewiring experiments and multiple-initiator cascade studies are prior art. None of the full-text primary works or compared exact claims found covers the simultaneous opposite-sign effect of the same single link across a common threshold with fixed seed, the five-decorated-class minimum, or the explicit three-cell all-n amplification. Searches are not novelty proofs; specific residual risks are listed.
residual_risks: Qualitative edge-dilution results are already known; no claim to their discovery is made. Independent bibliographic checking could find an equivalent exact finite census or unbounded same-edge reversal construction under complex contagion, social reinforcement, or tipping-point terminology.
The Oxford handbook chapter Diffusion in Networks (circa 2015) appears relevant from a short accessible excerpt but was not examined in full; no whole-document not-covering conclusion is drawn.
A 2014 multiplex threshold-cascade paper was accessible in abstract but not verified throughout; the multiplex mechanism is different, yet unseen supplements could contain related examples.
Finite enumeration certifies only orders through five; the arbitrary-size conclusion has its own direct proof, and no enumeration-based uniqueness is claimed for larger orders.

value.rationale: A single tie is an elementary intervention, and fractional-threshold social diffusion supplies two genuinely competing mechanisms: reinforcement through an additional path and dilution of the incumbent signals. The result identifies a sharp minimal network size and all initial mechanisms, then exhibits an arbitrarily large successful-cascade increase coexisting with an opposite effect at another behavioral threshold for exactly the same intervention and source. This is a motivated structural classification and scalable counterexample, not a cosmetic numeric bound; empirical validity is not claimed.
